title: Page 6
lines: 夜色的大氅覆在群山之上，浓云翻涌于天际。
四日前，代代由云取宫保管的阅魂录，遭不明人士盗出宫中，次日，云取宫宫主司徒勤于道家现任掌门清罡真人的监督下，自尽谢罪。
叶慈踩着沉重的步伐走向西宫深处，在这夜已深人未静的时分，沿途廊上灯火，在飒冷的西风中奄奄欲熄，将地上的身影摇曳成一抹孤单的游魂。他停下脚步远眺向东宫的方向，与清冷空旷的西宫相比，正在举行宫内大丧的东宫灯影幢幢人声沸腾，为此，他暗恨地握紧了掌心。
按神宫律令，每一代宫主仙逝后，神宫中的大祭司必须卜算出下一任转世宫主所在之处，并由神官派出旗下神捕去迎。可如今，三日了，宫中十位大祭司与百来位祭司无一动手卜算，反倒是齐聚在东宫中，围着司徒勤的独子司徒霜一同哭灵，而那位人称少宫主的司徒霜，不但腆着脸在神宫中以主人之姿主持大丧，大有取代下一任宫主之势。
居然妄想窃据不该属于他的宫主之位……那位收拢了祭司一派的少宫主，真以为无人知晓他暗地里干了什么？
当日在宫主司徒勤自尽前，司徒勤就已告知自己的神官叶润，将阅魂录一书盗出宫的主使人，不是他人，正是他的独子司徒霜所为，单就盗窃镇宫之宝此一罪，司徒霜就不得不死，可爱子心切的他，却还是选择一力承担，情愿赔上性命也不要这等神宫丑闻公诸于天下。
司徒勤的做法虽出于私心，但为了神宫着想，叶润也不得不赞同，只因此事若真告知天下，日后神宫还有何威信可言？而世人又将如何看待素来以医药卜巫救世的神宫？神宫数百年来的清誉，断不能毁在司徒霜一人的手上。
于是司徒勤死了，连带的，叶润也不得不死。
按制，同样也是采取转世制的神官，代代就是两两一对，两者之间的关系可谓主仆，亦可谓兄弟，一同转世，一同治理神宫，也因此，为追随宫主，一旦宫主死，神官，也得死。
叶慈恨恨地咬紧牙关，不断在心底问……
凭什么？
司徒勤要为子扛罪就算了，凭什么他的师父叶润也得为了司徒霜那个自卑又自大的小人枉死？凭什么就为了司徒霜一个人的贪婪，就得赔上叶润的性命？
不过就只是个宫主之子而已，既无实权又无实力，生来体弱不能从武，也不像神宫之人对医药或卜巫皆有天分，除了为宫主所生亲子之外，他以为他是个什么东西？明明就是个外人，却妄想在害死宫主后，以子承父业之名成为下一任新宫主？他以为神宫宫主与人间皇帝一样皆是世袭制？就凭他这个名不正言不顺的东西，也配与尊贵的转世宫主相提并论？
他作梦。
伸手推开西宫干元殿的大门，叶慈缓缓抬起眼眸，看着一殿围绕在叶润身旁的神捕们，皆红着眼眶朝他看过来。叶慈只觉得忽然间他的脚下沉重如石，令他往前的步子怎么也迈不开。
「小慈，过来。」身着一身神官正式吉服的叶润，端坐在高位上微笑地对他招手。
「……师父。」叶慈哑声应着，拖着脚步一步步走向他，脚下的每一行、每一踏，所走的彷佛不是寻常里已走惯的大殿，而是通往自家师尊死亡的泥淖。
「替他换装，还有去把东西取来。」像没看见他眼底所盛载的哀戚般，叶润转头向身旁的神捕们吩咐。
烛光灼灼明亮的大殿上，十五岁的少年眼底藏着眼泪，站在殿上任由沉默的神捕们为他换上神官正式吉服，并替他重新梳发，为他梳起神官特有的发髻，而两名年纪也不过十五六岁的小神捕，则是一人手捧着置有神官御印的玉盘，一人则两手捧着象征着神官地位的法剑。
待到都已打点齐全，叶润示意叶慈上前跪在座前，满意地瞧了瞧这名打小带到大的唯一弟子，一手轻轻抚上他年轻的脸庞。
「为师要走了，你身为神宫的下一任神官，在找到新宫主前，神宫就暂且拜托你了。」叶慈是他一手调教出来的，他很清楚这孩子的本事，更放心于他的沉着稳重。
叶慈咬着唇，努力不让泪水模糊了眼眶，他频眨着眼，试图想看清楚师父他那一如以往慈祥的脸庞，而这时，站在他身后的两个小神捕已忍不住哭了出来。
「呜呜……」与叶慈一块儿长大的松岗，哭得上气不接下气，几乎要捧不住手中的玉盘。
「我不服，这是凭什么……凭什么啊？」脾气较直率的朔方，边哭边忍不住抖着嗓子嚷出声，「那些大祭司怎么可以天天来催叶大人去死……叶大人又没有做错什么，他们怎么可以……」想起那些大祭司的嘴脸，他就恨不能提着刀，去东宫将那些手不能提肩不能挑，偏还坐享高位的大祭司都给砍过一轮。他就不懂，这是活生生的一个人啊，他们怎能那样指着叶叔叔的鼻子口口声声叫他快些去死，好陪伴已逝的宫主？
「别说了。」叶慈低声向他喝道。
「可是……」朔方不甘地看着他，却不意在他眼中见着了更深的恨意后，怔怔地张着嘴，忘了接下来想说的是什么。
「师父，您接着说。」叶慈深吸了口气，压抑下心头的翻涌，抬起头柔声地道。
叶润不舍地看着他那伪装坚强的模样，他知道，在场最无法接受自己死讯，偏又不能逃避的人就是叶慈，可他没有选择，主死仆身殉，是神宫历代以来不可违背的规矩，他再不舍得眼前的少年，他也得放手让叶慈独自一人挑起重担，哪怕未来是遍地荆棘还是疾风骤雨。
「你让宵小窃据，你得牢牢守住神宫数代大统。」司徒霜明晃晃的野心，可说是连遮掩也不遮掩一下，只是这神宫，又岂是他一个外人可贪图的？他也未免太小看这神宫数百年来传承下来的规矩了。
叶润一掌置于他的顶上，「为师这就把毕生功力传予你，你千万忍住。」
「师父……」至此叶慈再也忍不住，随着语调中泄漏出的哽咽，一颗逃窜的泪珠自他的眼眶翻落。
「好孩子，记得，未来的宫主需要你。」叶润不给他拒绝的余地，一把话说完便蓄起内劲，先是出手连点他十大保命穴脉，硬生生地将体内的武道根基拔起，强行为他灌顶。
神官体内建筑在武道之上的特有元力，宛如一道洪流自叶慈的顶上灌下，冲击他的四肢百骸之余，亦重新构筑起他的神智，代代相承的神官元力中隐藏的智慧与法则，庞大如海潮，过早塞进了他年幼的神智中，在充实了他之余，亦同时令他生不如死，缕缕的鲜血自叶慈的两耳中溢出，面上的血色尽数褪去，苍白得几乎透明。
殿上包围着他们师徒俩的神捕们，或无声流泪或紧闭双眼，无人愿去看那面上始终都带笑的叶润，也无人愿直视那个被迫一夜长大的少年。

随着时间一点一滴的逝去，殿上苦熬着的众人，从不觉得时间是如此漫长，他们不知道，在施与受之间，何者所受的痛苦较为摧心、何者又较折磨。他们只能无能为力的睁眼看着，随着传功的时间渐长，叶润的发丝渐渐由乌黑变得雪白，叶慈苍白的面容则是逐渐变得红润，随着宫外的天色亮起，原本温润如玉的叶润变得苍老消瘦，而叶慈则是体内生气勃勃，原本武力还是士级中阶的他，一鼓作气登堂迈入了相级初阶，体内蕴含的内劲变得更加浑厚沉稳。

Chapter 1(1)
The dark cloak of night hangs over the mountains, and thick clouds billow in the sky.
Four days ago, the Yuhunlu, which had been kept by Yunchui Palace for generations, was stolen from the palace by unknown persons. The next day, Situ Qin, the master of Yunchui Palace, committed suicide under the supervision of Qinggang Zhenren, the current head of Taoism.
Ye Ci walked towards the depths of the West Palace with heavy steps. In the dead of night, the lights on the corridors along the way were dying in the cold west wind, swaying the figure on the ground into a lonely wandering soul. He stopped and looked in the direction of the East Palace. Compared with the cold and empty West Palace, the East Palace, where a funeral was being held, was filled with lights, shadows and people. For this reason, he clenched his palms secretly.
According to the laws of the shrine, after each generation of palace lord dies, the high priest in the shrine must divine the location of the next reincarnated palace lord, and the priest will send his subordinates to greet him. But now, three days have passed, and none of the ten high priests and hundreds of priests in the palace have made fortunes. Instead, they have gathered in the East Palace, weeping together around Situ Qin's only son Situ Shuang. Situ Shuang, known as the young palace master, not only presided over the funeral in the palace with a shy face as a master, but also had the potential to replace the next palace master.
He actually wanted to steal the palace master position that didn't belong to him... The young palace master who had gathered the priests' faction, really thought that no one knew what he was doing secretly?
Before the palace owner Situ Qin committed suicide that day, Situ Qin had informed his priest Ye Run that the person responsible for stealing the Soul Reading Book out of the palace was none other than his only son Situ Shuang. For the crime of stealing the palace's treasure, Situ Shuang had to die. Although he was eager for his beloved son, he still chose to bear the responsibility and would rather lose his life than let the scandal of the palace be made public to the world.
Although Situ Qin's actions were selfish, for the sake of the shrine, Ye Run had to agree. If this matter was really told to the world, what prestige would the shrine have in the future? And how will the world view the shrine, which has always used medicine, divination, and witchcraft to save the world? The centuries-old reputation of the shrine cannot be destroyed by Situ Shuang alone.
So Situ Qin died, and Ye Run also had to die.
According to the system, the priests also adopt the reincarnation system. From generation to generation, they are paired in pairs. The relationship between the two can be called master and servant, or brothers. They are reincarnated together and manage the temple together. Therefore, in order to follow the palace master, once the palace master dies, the priest must also die.
Ye Ci gritted his teeth bitterly and kept asking in his heart...
Why?
Situ Qin had to bear the blame for his son, so why did his master Ye Run have to die in vain for Situ Shuang, a villain with low self-esteem and arrogance? Why should Ye Run's life be sacrificed just for Situ Shuang's greed?
He was just the son of the palace lord. He had no real power or strength. He was born too weak to engage in martial arts. He was not as talented in medicine or divination as the people in the palace. Apart from being the son of the palace lord, what did he think he was? He is obviously an outsider, but he wants to become the next new palace lord in the name of inheriting his father's legacy after killing the palace lord? He thought that the palace masters of the shrines were hereditary just like the human emperors? Just because he has such an unfair name, is he worthy to be compared with the noble reincarnated palace master?
He dreams.
Reaching out to push open the door of Qianyuan Hall in the West Palace, Ye Ci slowly raised his eyes and looked at the gods surrounding Ye Run in the hall. They all looked towards him with red eyes. Ye Ci felt that suddenly his feet were as heavy as stone, making it impossible for him to move forward.
"Xiao Ci, come here." Ye Run, who was wearing a formal priest's uniform, sat on a high seat and waved to him with a smile.
"...Master." Ye Ci responded hoarsely, dragging his feet towards him step by step. Every step and step under his feet seemed not to be the hall he was used to walking in, but the mud leading to his master's death.
"Change his clothes, and go get his things." As if he didn't see the sadness in his eyes, Ye Run turned to give instructions to the magicians beside him.
"Yes."
In the candlelit hall, a fifteen-year-old boy had tears hidden in his eyes. He stood in the hall and allowed the silent gods to put him into the official priest's robes, comb his hair again, and style his hair into a priest's unique bun. One of the two young gods, only fifteen or sixteen years old, was holding a jade plate with the priest's royal seal in his hand, and the other was holding a magic sword in both hands that symbolized the priest's status.
When everything was done, Ye Run motioned Ye Ci to come forward and kneel in front of the seat. He looked at the only disciple who had been brought up from childhood with satisfaction and gently touched his young face with one hand.
"My master is about to leave. As the next priest of the Shrine, the Shrine will be entrusted to you for the time being until a new master is found." Ye Ci was trained by him. He knew the child's abilities very well and was more assured of his composure.
Ye Ci bit his lip, trying not to let tears blur his eyes. He blinked frequently, trying to see his master's kind face as before, but at this time, the two little gods standing behind him couldn't help crying.
"Aww..." Songgang, who grew up with Ye Ci, was crying so hard that he could hardly hold the jade plate in his hand.
"I don't accept it. Why...why?" Shuo Fang, who had a more outspoken temper, couldn't help shouting at the top of his voice while crying, "How can those high priests come every day to urge Mr. Ye to die... Mr. Ye has done nothing wrong, how can they..." Thinking of the faces of those high priests, he wished he could go to the East Palace with a knife and chop off all the high priests who could not lift their hands or shoulders, but still sat in high positions. He didn't understand, this was a living person, how could they point at Uncle Ye's nose and keep telling him to die quickly so that they could accompany the deceased palace master?
"Stop talking." Ye Ci whispered to him.
"But..." Shuofang looked at him reluctantly, but unexpectedly saw deeper hatred in his eyes, and opened his mouth in confusion, forgetting what he wanted to say next.
"Master, please continue." Ye Ci took a deep breath, suppressed the turmoil in his heart, raised his head and said softly.
Ye Run reluctantly looked at his pretended to be strong. He knew that the person present who could not accept the news of his death the most and could not escape was Ye Ci, but he had no choice. The master died and the servant sacrificed himself. This was a rule that could not be violated in the past generations of the shrine. No matter how reluctant he was to let go of the young man in front of him, he had to let Ye Ci shoulder the burden alone, even if the future was full of thorns or storms.
"You let Xiao Xiao steal the throne, and you have to firmly guard the power of the shrine for generations." Situ Shuang's obvious ambition can be said to be unconcealed. But this shrine, how can he, an outsider, covet it? He also underestimated the rules passed down by this palace for hundreds of years.
"Yes."
Ye Run put a palm on his head, "As my teacher, I will pass on my lifelong skills to you. You must hold back."
"Master..." At this point, Ye Ci could no longer hold back. With the choking leaking from his tone, a fleeing teardrop fell from his eye.
"Good boy, remember, the future palace master needs you." Ye Run didn't give him any room to refuse. As soon as he finished speaking, he gathered up his inner strength. He first touched his ten life-saving acupuncture points, forcibly uprooted the martial arts foundation in his body, and forcibly initiated him.
The unique Yuan Power built on martial arts in the priest's body was like a torrent pouring down from the top of Ye Ci's head. While impacting his limbs and bones, it also rebuilt his sanity. The wisdom and law hidden in the Priest's Yuan Power passed down from generation to generation Then, it was as huge as the ocean tide, which was prematurely stuffed into his young mind. While enriching him, it also made his life worse than death. Strands of blood overflowed from Ye Ci's ears, and all the blood on his face faded, becoming pale and almost transparent.
The masters who surrounded the master and apprentice in the hall were either crying silently or closing their eyes tightly. No one wanted to look at Ye Run, who always had a smile on his face, and no one wanted to look directly at the young man who was forced to grow up overnight.
As time passed bit by bit, the people suffering in the palace never felt that time was so long. They did not know that between giving and receiving, which one suffered more heart-breaking pain and which one was more torturous. They could only open their eyes and watch helplessly. As the time of passing on the skills went on, Ye Run's hair gradually turned from black to snow-white, and Ye Ci's pale face gradually turned rosy. As the sky outside the palace lit up, Ye Run, who was originally as gentle as jade, became old and thin, while Ye Ci was full of vitality in his body. His original martial arts was still at the middle level of the sergeant level. He stepped into the early stage of the phase level in one go, and the inner energy contained in his body became more vigorous and steady.
